new_entities.name: Nutrigenomic personalized nutrition
new_entities.description: Dietary guidance tailored partly or primarily using genomic or nutrigenomic information.

new_entities.name: Diet outcomes
new_entities.description: Changes in dietary intake, diet quality, adherence, or related nutrition-behavior measures.

edges.effect_quant: The Food4Me trial found that personalized nutrition improved dietary behavior more than conventional advice at 6 months, but adding genotype data on top of diet and phenotype information did not clearly produce a large extra effect. Later systematic reviews likewise conclude that personalized nutrition can improve some dietary outcomes, but benefits are inconsistent and the genotype-specific increment remains modest.
edges.population: generally healthy adults receiving personalized or nutrigenomic dietary advice through digital, clinic, or research programs
edges.mechanism: Tailored advice may improve engagement, relevance, and adherence, but the behavior-change advantage may come more from personalization itself than from nutrigenomic precision per se.
edges.summary: This is a cautiously positive but still mixed edge. Personalized nutrition can help some people improve diet quality or nutrient intake, yet the specific value added by nutrigenomic/genotype information is often small, inconsistent, or hard to isolate.
edges.caveats: Better outcomes in personalized nutrition trials do not automatically validate direct-to-consumer nutrigenomic panels. Much of the benefit may derive from coaching intensity, self-monitoring, and tailored feedback rather than gene-based inference alone.

evidence.citation: Jinnette R et al 2021 Adv Nutr
evidence.notes: Does Personalized Nutrition Advice Improve Dietary Intake in Healthy Adults? A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
